judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the first 'Thomann News' teaser card, a link to youtube.com/watch?v=7aDSIaFjkXM named 'YouTube Marie Leloup plays Golden from "Kpop Demon Hunters" in the new Thomann Shop!'. The third card (Bx3MLITMdtM) has the same name apart from letter case. The finding's facts are right: the names match, the URLs differ, and no programmatic context sets them apart. But Rampa never read the destinations. Both are Thomann Music videos with exactly these titles and the same description, showing the same performance: the first is a 31-second Short and the second the full 195-second video. Each link's text is the title of the video it opens, which Understanding 2.4.4 calls sufficient to describe a link's purpose. That document lists different text for different destinations only as a best practice. The ACT rule for 2.4.4 (fd3a94, still only proposed) passes links that lead to equivalent resources. Its definition says such resources may differ in how much information they hold, so long as the key content they advertise (this performance) is the same. A user can tell what either link does. The only thing the text does not reveal is which one is the short clip, and the visible text does not tell sighted users that either. Some auditors would still flag the duplicate as a 2.4.4 problem. The thumbnails' empty alt text is a separate question, not this claim. The live page still had both links on 2026-10-11.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the third 'Thomann News' teaser card, a link to youtube.com/watch?v=Bx3MLITMdtM named 'YouTube Marie Leloup plays Golden from "KPop Demon Hunters" in the new Thomann Shop!'. It matches the first card (7aDSIaFjkXM) except for letter case. As the finding says, the URLs differ and nothing in the programmatic context tells the two apart. But Rampa did not read the destinations. They are the same Marie Leloup performance on Thomann's channel, with the same title and description: this one is the full 3:15 video and the other is a 31-second Short. The link text is the destination video's own title, which Understanding 2.4.4 accepts as describing a link's purpose. It treats different text for different destinations only as a best practice. Under the ACT definition of equivalent resources, which allows the resources to differ in how much information they hold, the proposed ACT rule fd3a94 would likely pass the pair. The purpose of the link (watch this performance on YouTube) can be determined. The unstated Short-or-full-video distinction is not shown in visible text to anyone either. Reasonable auditors could flag the duplicate, but it is not a clear failure of 2.4.4. The live page was unchanged on 2026-10-11.
